newsitem.title: UK: UK opposition leaders demand parliament stays on.
newsitem.headline: UK opposition leaders demand parliament stays on.

text.p: Leaders of the main British opposition parties on Wednesday united behind a motion calling for parliament not to be prorogued on Friday as planned.
They said this could allow publication of a report on allegations that four Conservative MPs took cash from Harrod owner Mohammed Al-Fayed to ask parliamentary questions.

The motion, signed by Labour leader Tony Blair, Paddy Ashdown of the Liberal Democrats and the leaders of the Scottish and Welsh Nationalist parties, said prorogation, or the ending of parliamentary activities, should be deferred "for the good of our parliamentary system and in the public interest".
The motion has virtually no chance of being debated in the few hours remaining before prorogation is due to take effect.

But Ashdown said it would allow Prime Minister John Major to reconsider his decision to go for prorogation almost six weeks before a general election, an unusually long period. -- London Newsroom +44 171 5427767
